name: Parties and Date
title: Parties and Date

legal_basis.note: A contract of indemnity is one by which one party promises to save the other from loss caused to him by the conduct of the promisor himself or of any other person
An indemnity bond is chargeable with stamp duty at the rate prescribed by the State

source: Indian Contract Act, 1872; Indian Stamp Act, 1899
statutory_reference: Indian Contract Act, 1872 - S.124; Indian Stamp Act, 1899 - Schedule I Article 34
authoring_note: A bond is unilateral: the Obligor binds himself and the Beneficiary does not sign. The successors wording matters because an indemnity that dies with the Obligor is often not what was intended. Stamp duty on an indemnity bond is a State subject and the rate varies considerably; the advocate should confirm the rate and whether the instrument requires registration in the State of execution.
